items.title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
items.summary: Amazon researchers published HOPE (Higher-Order Pruning of Experts) on November 9, 2026, a technique that selects experts to remove from mixture-of-experts language models while accounting for how pairs of experts cooperate. The team reports the best mean ranking among five pruning methods and an illustrative SWE-Bench Pro result of 42.3 after 50% pruning versus 41.8 for the original model. Those scores apply to specified models and tasks, not a guaranteed 50% reduction in total production costs.

items.title: Copilot code review: API management and review overview updates
items.summary: GitHub's November 6, 2026 Copilot Code Review update added REST and GraphQL configuration controls from enterprise policy to repositories, clearer attribution of AI review comments and review-effort metadata. New review summaries also group skipped or excluded files. These are product-management capabilities; they do not mean AI approval is a replacement for human code review or security testing.

items.title: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is generally available and more
items.summary: GitHub announced general availability of the @GitHub coding-agent integration in Slack and Microsoft Teams on November 6, 2026. Team members can discuss bugs, initiate coding tasks, create issues and open pull requests from chat. Teams Canvas adds an in-conversation area for plans, diffs and previews. The feature does not grant unrestricted repository permissions or eliminate human code review.

items.title: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
items.summary: Ai2 introduced ToyBlocks on November 6, 2026 as a controllable simulated world for robot learning and evaluation. The release reports 85,336 demonstrations containing almost 1,600 hours and 144 million frames, spanning block-manipulation tasks and tests of generalization. Its simulated and limited physical-arm evaluations do not prove reliable manipulation in uncontrolled environments.

items.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
items.summary: OpenAI announced a partnership with Hacktron on November 6, 2026 to investigate security weaknesses in OpenAI systems, particularly where they connect to third-party services. Hacktron gains expanded access to frontier security models through Daybreak Red. This is an authorized research collaboration, not proof that a specific vulnerability count has been discovered or that all connected systems have been fixed.

items.title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
items.summary: OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench on November 6, 2026 with biotech partner Ligo, using 100 routine wet-lab tasks built from raw scientific evidence. At the highest compared reasoning setting GPT-6 Astra earned 66.7% mean rubric credit versus 43.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol. These are partial-credit benchmark averages, not percentages of experiments safely completed without scientific oversight.

items.title: Egyptian and Nigerian English join the Open ASR Leaderboard
items.summary: Hugging Face and Liva AI announced on November 6, 2026 that the Open ASR Leaderboard's private test set now includes spontaneous Egyptian-accented and Nigerian-accented English speech. The added conversational datasets are 1.34 and 1.55 hours respectively, and the leaderboard introduces comparisons between U.S., non-U.S. and international accent groupings. This improves evaluation coverage but does not prove speech systems are equally accurate across accents.

items.title: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
items.summary: NVIDIA published four specialized Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoints on November 5, 2026 for interactive simulation: Transfer-Auto, Sim-Auto, Sim-Transfer and Sim-Bimanual. They target multi-camera driving data, synchronized LiDAR, simulator-to-video rendering and two-arm robot interactions. The weights are available under OpenMDW1.1 terms, but publication does not validate autonomous driving or robot safety.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.summary: Google unveiled Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash on November 5, 2026 with native video clips of 3–15 seconds, conversational editing and improved reference consistency. The company says 720p video is priced at $0.07 per second, 30% lower than Omni 1.1. These are announced generation prices and product capabilities, not guaranteed cost per usable commercial video.

items.title: Detecting signs of hypertension using wearable sensors
items.summary: A peer-reviewed Nature study reported on November 5, 2026 that a Google Research system combined smartwatch optical and motion signals to screen for persistent hypertension without cuff calibration. In a prospective five-center study of 196 adults, sensitivity was 65.8% and specificity 90.0% against 24-hour ambulatory blood-pressure monitoring. This is a screening research result, not a substitute for a diagnostic cuff or clinical advice.

items.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber on November 5, 2026 as a specialized security research model for authorized vulnerability discovery and validation. In its tests, it reports 48.5% on ExploitGym versus 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and stronger adherence to assigned scope. Initial access is limited to approved Daybreak Red customers, so this is not a general ChatGPT model release.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure
items.summary: OpenAI published a National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint on November 5, 2026. The company promises that future compute campuses it owns and operates will pay their own electricity and grid-infrastructure costs, disclose site-level water and power use, and restrict NDAs with public officials. The separate blueprint proposes wider policy rules; neither document proves lower local electricity bills or creates new law.

items.title: A Closer Look at Phonon TTS. Launching High-Quality On-Device Speech That Tops the Benchmarks.
items.summary: A November 5, 2026 Hugging Face article introduced Phonon TTS, a small text-to-speech model family developed for local or on-device generation. It describes streaming speech, voice characteristics and comparative quality evaluations. These are the authors' claims and examples, not evidence of identical real-time performance, quality or licensing on every device.

items.title: Franklin Templeton uses OpenAI to support investment research
items.summary: Franklin Templeton described work with OpenAI tools on November 5, 2026 to support its investment research, initially concentrating on equities. Teams are developing workflows to compare viewpoints, test investment risks and bring continuously updated context to portfolio managers. The source is a corporate customer case study, not a controlled demonstration of improved investment returns or a launch of an autonomous trading system.

items.title: GitHub Copilot is now available in Xcode’s coding assistant
items.summary: GitHub announced on November 4, 2026 that GitHub Copilot is available in public preview in Xcode's built-in coding assistant, expanding the AI coding workflow for Apple-platform developers. The changelog describes an integration and its preview availability; it does not establish that every developer can access it or that generated apps are reliable without testing.

items.title: Agile Deliberation: How AI helps humans define the gray areas
items.summary: Google Research introduced Agile Deliberation on November 4, 2026, a framework that helps people define subjective image categories through discussion, difficult borderline examples and automatic prompt refinement. Eighteen live, 90-minute user sessions suggested improved classification and reduced effort compared with manual approaches in two domains. The study does not establish universally objective definitions for concepts such as healthy food or misleading promotional images.

items.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.
items.summary: OpenAI announced on November 4, 2026 that it intends to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc., describing the move as a way to expand developer tools for building, understanding and reviewing code through Codex. The announcement does not establish that the transaction has closed or that a combined product is already available.

items.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
items.summary: OpenAI reported on November 4, 2026 that an autonomous security research pipeline screened 2,308 candidate findings in selected Linux kernel code, dynamically reproduced 1,724 and developed distinct patches for 948 local privilege-escalation issues. The single research campaign used roughly $1.21 million in API credits. These are provider-reported results, not 948 already merged upstream fixes.

items.title: Introducing Images 2.6
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Images 2.6 on November 4, 2026 for ChatGPT, Codex and its API. It reports image generation up to 50% faster than the previous release, adds animated GIFs and sharper editing controls, and offers two API models: speed-focused Flare and detail-focused Sunburst. Provider performance claims are not guarantees for every request.

items.title: Dependabot version updates support Agent Package Manager
items.summary: GitHub added Agent Package Manager (APM) support to Dependabot version updates on November 3, 2026. It can open pull requests for supported Git-based skills, prompts and agent instruction dependencies declared in apm.yml, refreshing apm.lock.yaml if that file exists. This is version-update support only—not automatic vulnerability alerts or proof that updated agent instructions are safe.

items.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
items.summary: Ai2 published StateBench on November 3, 2026 to study how language models track changing facts through long sequences of assignments. Its researchers report major failures for frontier models on the hardest general-finite tests, with accuracy of 13% or below at the longest tested lengths in that specific experimental setup.

items.title: OpenAI Says ChatGPT Search-Like Queries Are About 20% of Google's
items.summary: In a first-hand interview published November 3, 2026, OpenAI consumer product lead Adam Fry estimated that ChatGPT handles search-like questions at roughly one-fifth of Google's query volume. OpenAI did not publish an independent comparison dataset, and the statement cannot be treated as a confirmed 20% search-market share or web referral figure.

items.title: Google Announces K-12 AI Search Controls and Guided Learning
items.summary: Google announced on November 3, 2026 that Search, Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Gemini in Classroom will be off by default for managed K-12 student accounts until an administrator enables access. Guided Learning is available globally in Classroom, while a separate Search pilot is planned for selected U.S. schools later in November.

items.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world
items.summary: OpenAI reported on November 3, 2026 that two employees used GPT-6 Astra to design a Codex-connected hardware prototype, including enclosure, printed circuit board, interface and firmware, in under a week. A manufacturer made a small batch within a month, but human reviews and changes were still necessary to handle real manufacturing constraints.

items.title: Transformers Model Integration Contracts
items.summary: Hugging Face outlined Model Integration Contracts (MICs) on November 3, 2026, proposing small architecture-aware model fixtures, runnable usage paths and human-reviewed baselines for faster CI checks. A retrospective UMT5 replay caught a real regression, but the MIC job is currently advisory and full-checkpoint testing still matters.

items.title: CWE-bench v2: More coverage, quality, and transparency
items.summary: Collinear AI introduced CWE-bench v2 on November 3, 2026, using 100 runnable tasks from real open-source projects to evaluate agent-written security fixes. Its report compares 11 models and lists Gemini 4 Argon at 67.8% pass@1 and Claude Opus 5.5 at 67.3%, within the benchmark's specific testing setup rather than all real-world vulnerability repair.

items.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI described Pando on November 2, 2026, a Git-compatible backend serving its monorepo under heavy Codex-driven concurrent development. OpenAI reports nearly fivefold lower median push latency and close to a petabyte of Git data delivered daily, but the figures describe its production environment rather than independent benchmarks for other teams.

items.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
items.summary: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on November 2, 2026, outlining how future compute campuses could reduce electricity demand during grid stress. Its Effingham County agreement with Georgia Power includes up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response, but campus operation, savings and customer-rate effects remain future claims subject to implementation.

items.title: LifeVal
items.summary: OpenAI introduced LifeVal on November 2, 2026 to assess AI assistance on practical tasks such as childcare, household administration, personal finance and public services. Its task selection draws on time-use research and a 3,995-person survey; published examples are evaluation results, not guarantees of real-world completion.

items.title: Community safety report and new protections for teens
items.summary: OpenAI is strengthening violence prevention in ChatGPT with expanded safeguards, earlier interventions, and a new commitment to public safety reporting.

items.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
items.summary: OpenAI’s updated Model Spec outlines five core values to guide more capable AI toward sound judgment, human agency, and faithfulness to human intent.

items.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
items.summary: OpenAI uses layered monitoring to detect frontier model misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior so responders can intervene before incidents escalate.

items.title: Introducing AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel: Open Models for Speech and Decisions on Apple Platforms
items.summary: AnySpeechRecognizer extends Apple's SpeechAnalyzer workflow with local Core ML engines including Parakeet and Qwen3-ASR plus up to four-speaker diarization. AnyDecisionModel offers typed Swift probability, choice and score outputs. The published recognition benchmarks are Mac-only and licenses vary by checkpoint.

items.title: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work
items.summary: Microsoft introduced the Copilot harness in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service as a public preview on October 28, 2026. Teams can configure agents using reusable skills, connected tools and MCP integrations while Foundry runs the agent loop and sandbox. The preview differs from the generally available long-running resilience feature for hosted agents, and the harness has its own regional, model and billing constraints.

items.title: Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion
items.summary: GitHub Copilot Fusion is generally available. Instead of picking a model for each task, choose Copilot Fusion and let Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate which models it uses for you.…

items.title: GitHub intelligence puts your code, context, and history to work
items.summary: GitHub announced that Copilot Memory is generally available for paid Copilot plans on October 28, 2026. The GitHub intelligence release also introduces Copilot Dreaming in public preview, which can refine memories and propose repository instruction updates, plus contextual code search across repositories. The three capabilities differ in availability, opt-in requirements and administrative controls; they should not be described as one universally enabled feature.

items.title: Build shared workflows for your team with Copilot Automations
items.summary: Shared Copilot Automations are rolling out, enabling teams to build and maintain AI-powered workflows together. With Copilot Automations, you can combine prompts, triggers, and tools to design workflows around the…

items.title: Generate and edit images directly in Copilot
items.summary: You can now generate and edit images using natural language in GitHub Copilot. When you ask for an image, your selected reasoning model calls a dedicated image-generation tool powered by…

items.title: AI for Science expands to foundations and research institutions
items.summary: Anthropic expanded AI for Science on October 28, 2026, highlighting 20 foundations, research institutions and scientific groups receiving or distributing Claude credits. The initiative supports access to AI tools and projects across several scientific fields; it does not establish that a new drug, cure or scientific breakthrough has been validated.

Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
items.summary: Anthropic and the U.S. General Services Administration expanded their OneGov agreement on October 27, 2026, offering a 40% discount on eligible consumption-based Claude model and API usage for government organizations. GSA confirms no minimum purchase commitment and access across federal, state, local and tribal governments, through approved procurement routes. Anthropic separately describes expanded enterprise and government product discounts; buyers must verify the exact applicable offer and channel.

items.summary: OpenAI shares model results on the Kakeya conjecture, Exponential Time Hypothesis, and quantum chromodynamics—and how researchers can verify and build on them.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit strengthen security across complex codebases
items.summary: CodeRabbit uses GPT-6.1 Sol to investigate security risks across complex codebases. Its security agent helps developers review findings and proposed fixes.

items.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
items.summary: OpenAI describes defense-in-depth controls for frontier model training and evaluation: an offline cached web environment, container-plus-microVM isolation, monitoring and network boundaries. A high-compute red team found real sandbox escapes and egress paths, leading to patches before RL training resumed on October 1.

items.title: Anima helps clinics cut call waits by 75% with GPT-6 and GPT-Live
items.summary: Anima expands what care teams can do with OpenAI models, giving them more capacity to respond to patients.

items.title: Build more responsive apps with the Decisions API
items.summary: OpenAI's Decisions API is generally available for bounded decision questions using GPT-6 Luna. It supports predicate probabilities, predefined choices and ordered scores, with text, image or JSON context; up to 400 questions can be sent per request. Vendor and customer speed claims should not be treated as independent benchmarks.

items.title: Using thousands of AI agents to uncover new leads in biological data
items.summary: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research used thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents to interrogate a whole-brain mouse CRISPR atlas spanning millions of cells in 32 minutes. Distributed analysis brought together gene perturbations, literature and hypotheses; a controlled comparison showed over 700 literature references versus 11 from a single agent at the largest workload.
